brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not reach its model to produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1005683 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 4.2s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 1005683) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout is at 0% success (120/120 failed) with $18,400/min revenue at risk and only 60s tolerance [BIZ-4]. The root blocker pid 1005683 is idle in transaction for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1 [DB-1], indicating a stuck/abandoned session not actively processing. No protected settlements in flight [DB-2], no change-calendar protection [BIZ-3]. Although adhoc_reporting is not in the workload registry (owner/cost unknown) [BIZ-2, BIZ-5], the session appears stuck and the cost of inaction (complete checkout outage) is known and maximal. Memory shows terminating a stuck batch workload previously restored checkout to 100% [MEM-1].

audit.report: Checkout degraded when database session pid 1005683 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting) sat idle in transaction for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, holding a lock that 12 sessions waited on. Checkout success dropped from 53% (32/60 over 15s) to 0% (120/120 failed over 30s) against a 95% SLO, placing about $18,400/min of revenue at risk within a 60s degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian proposed terminating adhoc_reporting after verifying no protected settlements were in flight and no change-calendar window applied, though adhoc_reporting was absent from the workload registry so its interruption cost was unknown. The Continuity Guardian could not reach its model provider to review the proposal, so the pact escalated to on-call after one round (399.5s) and the termination was not executed. The business is not back: checkout stayed at 0% success and the incident remains escalated.
audit.root_cause: An idle adhoc_reporting session (pid 1005683) held a database lock that starved checkout, and the proposed kill was never executed because the Continuity Guardian's model provider was unreachable, forcing escalation.
lessons: Register adhoc_reporting in biz.workload_registry with an owner and interruption cost so the Continuity Guardian can judge whether to terminate a blocking session instead of escalating.
Pre-approve terminating idle-in-transaction adhoc_reporting sessions that block checkout when success falls below SLO, since the business tolerates only 60s of degradation and $18,400/min is at risk.
Add a model-provider fallback or hard timeout for Continuity Guardian review so an unreachable provider cannot delay adhoc_reporting lock resolution past the business tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian did not waste a round; it probed the workload registry, protected settlements, and change calendar before re-proposing termination with full evidence. The Continuity Guardian missed its review round entirely because its model provider failed, so no invariant overrode the proposal—the process simply failed closed on a missing review.
follow_ups: Page on-call to terminate pid 1005683, clear the lock, and confirm checkout returns to the 95% SLO.
Add adhoc_reporting to the workload registry with owner and cost.
Configure a Continuity Guardian model-provider fallback or timeout so future reviews do not block past 60s.

proposal.rationale: Root blocker pid 1005683 is batch_worker/adhoc_reporting idle in transaction for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1 [DB-1], indicating a stuck/abandoned session not actively processing. Checkout success is 53-74% vs 95% SLO with $4,748/min revenue at risk and only 60s tolerance [TEL-1, BIZ-1]. Ad-hoc reporting workloads are typically interruptible and lower priority than checkout. Memory shows terminating a batch workload previously restored checkout [MEM-1], though that was a different workload (inventory_reconcile). Need registry/tradeoff data to confirm replayability and cost.
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating the idle-in-transaction session releases its locks, unblocking the 1 directly blocked session and potentially the 12 total waiting sessions [DB-1]. Checkout latency should recover as lock contention clears. Database returns to normal lock state.
proposal.risk_assessment: If the ad-hoc reporting session was mid-transaction with uncommitted writes, those would roll back (but last statement is SELECT 1, suggesting read-only). If the workload is not replayable or has high replay cost, owner may object. Protected settlements in flight could be affected (unknown, need probe). Change calendar may restrict termination during deployments.
